clue.text: Wool used more in knitting

indicators.note: knitting works strands together into a new pattern, so the letters of these two words are reworked

explanation.surface: A knitter gets through more wool when making a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Merino is a fine wool from the sheep breed of that name.

clue.text: Top — step up to it in time

indicators.note: in tells us the pieces before it sit inside the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for step is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a pace is a single step
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to step up to the top in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like a noun but is the slang verb meaning to kill; 'up' turns the step backwards in this down clue before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To top someone is slang for killing them, and beheading is one specific way of doing that.

clue.text: Certain one can't be

parts.note: read as a person who cannot be certain, one who holds that the existence of God is unknowable

explanation.surface: A remark that some particular person is unable to exist.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone of this view holds that nothing can be known for sure about God, so cannot be certain.

clue.text: Dismay at increase in eastern currency

indicators.note: in places the word for increase inside the currency

parts.note: the sen is a small coin in several East Asian currencies
to add is to increase

explanation.surface: Someone is dismayed by a rise in the value of an Asian currency.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismay someone is to make them unhappy, a close synonym of the verb in the grid.

clue.text: Hit and run without due care

parts.note: to slap is to hit
to dash is to run

explanation.surface: A hit-and-run driver acted with reckless disregard.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is careless and hurried, done without due care.

clue.text: Vote on act affecting Monica, as they say

definitions.note: Monica sounds like moniker, slang for a name, so the definition is something that changes one's name

indicators.note: on tells us one piece is joined onto the other to make the whole

parts.note: a deed is an act
a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: A vote on some legislation is said to involve a woman called Monica.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as they say' points at the sound of Monica, which is moniker, slang for a name; the definition is an adjectival phrase describing the legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed poll is the British legal document by which a person formally changes their name.

clue.text: Student taking some English afterward has to protract

parts.note: L for learner, a student driver's plate
Eng is the short form of English, part of the word
then means afterward

explanation.surface: A student taking an English course afterwards has to stay on longer.
explanation.definitionFit: To protract something is to draw it out or make it longer in time.

clue.text: Hardwoods called for a trick?

indicators.note: called hints at a word spoken, so we want what sounds like the trees

parts.note: oaks are hardwood trees

explanation.surface: A question whether certain timbers were wanted for a prank.
explanation.walkthrough: The trees said with an extra initial H give the sound of the answer, a playful inversion of dropping an aitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoax is a deception or practical joke, the same thing as a trick.

clue.text: Died — to have been born first is a requirement

indicators.note: first puts the word for born before the abbreviation for died

parts.note: née, French for born, introduces a woman's maiden name
d is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A grim remark that one must be born before one can die.
explanation.definitionFit: A need is something required, a requirement.

clue.text: Fish with beer and plonk

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
plonk is cheap wine, and vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: A meal of fish washed down with beer and cheap wine.
explanation.definitionFit: An alevin is a young salmon or trout just hatched, so a kind of fish.

clue.text: Get wise about damaged boat's possible cause

indicators.note: about means the word for wise goes round the rest

parts.note: sage means wise

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of the vessel are knocked out of order

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter, just the vessel

explanation.surface: Learn the truth about what probably wrecked a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' gives BOTA, and 'about' wraps the wise word round it; the whole clue also hints at why a vessel might be wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberate wrecking is a plausible explanation for damage, making it a possible cause.

clue.text: One's certificate is in abstinence — from candour?

definitions.text: One's certificate is in abstinence — from candour?

parts.note: a diploma is a certificate

indicators.note: in places the small word inside the letters for abstinence

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means abstaining from alcohol
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question whether a person's qualification lies in holding back from frankness.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the person: their qualification is in refraining from candour, that is, tact.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomatist is a diplomat, one whose skill lies in tactful restraint rather than blunt honesty.

clue.text: Wilson's attitudes?

parts.note: refers to a 1956 novel by Angus Wilson whose title is this word followed by Attitudes

explanation.surface: A question about the views of someone named Wilson.
explanation.definitionFit: Angus Wilson wrote Anglo-Saxon Attitudes, so this word completes his novel's title before attitudes.

clue.text: Worker with poor rate when working?

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A labourer complains about low pay while on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: An operator is someone who works a machine, so a worker.

clue.text: Riches of clue open to doubt

indicators.note: open to doubt suggests the letters are unsettled and can be reordered

explanation.surface: A setter admits a clue about wealth is ambiguous.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence is great wealth or luxury, which is what riches means.

clue.text: Trade done treacherously downstream?

parts.note: evokes the idiom of betraying someone by sending them down the river

explanation.surface: Commerce conducted dishonestly along a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling is trade, and selling someone down the river means betraying them.

clue.text: Where Strauss may add to the score

definitions.meaning: Andrew Strauss, England cricket captain, batted at the crease
to raise a total by adding to it

explanation.surface: An England batsman piles on runs from his usual spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Strauss was an England cricket captain; the crease is the marked line where a batsman stands, and split as two words the answer says where he is.
explanation.definitionFit: To increase a score is to add to it, and split in two the answer says where a batsman stands.

clue.text: After heaving coal the old man needs something stronger

indicators.note: heaving tosses the letters of the fuel about

parts.note: pop is a familiar name for one's father

explanation.surface: After shovelling coal, Dad wants a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heaving' gives the scrambled fuel first; 'After' is only a joining word. The drink is called stronger because it is spiked soda.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcopop is a sweet fizzy drink laced with alcohol, stronger than plain soda.

clue.text: It's unhealthy for Piggott in school, but not at first

indicators.note: in puts the jockey's first name inside the shortened school
not at first removes the opening letter of the word for school

parts.note: taken as written before its first letter goes
Lester Piggott was a famous English flat-racing jockey

explanation.surface: Something is bad for the jockey Piggott at school.
explanation.walkthrough: Lester Piggott was a celebrated British flat-racing jockey; 'not at first' leaves CHOOL, and 'in' sets his first name inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: High blood levels of this fatty substance are bad for the heart, so it is something unhealthy.

clue.text: Vegetable pot found in dump

indicators.note: found in places the vessel inside the word for dump

parts.note: a tip is a rubbish dump
an urn is a pot or vase

explanation.surface: A vegetable pot turns up at the rubbish tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnip is a root vegetable.

clue.text: Smart but faint-hearted, lacking knowledge

indicators.note: lacking means the word for knowledge is removed

parts.note: chicken means cowardly
ken is knowledge, as in beyond one's ken

explanation.surface: Someone stylish but timid and ignorant.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken means range of knowledge, mainly Scottish and northern English.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and fashionable, which is one sense of smart.

clue.text: So, presumably, I'm there to speak in passing water?

indicators.note: to speak tells us the answer is how a reply to the opening words would sound

parts.note: if I'm there, the reply is you're here, said with the aitch dropped

explanation.surface: Someone arriving somewhere, mentioned while crossing a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Answer someone who says 'I'm there' and you say "you're 'ere", with the aitch dropped; the definition is a phrase saying where the compound is found.
explanation.definitionFit: Urea is a compound excreted in urine, so it is found in what is passed.

clue.text: Centaur

parts.note: the mythical creature is part horse, part man, so read its two halves together

explanation.definitionFit: A centaur combines a horse's body with a man's torso, and the term also means a rider.

clue.text: Professional weight is of little matter

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A professional says weight is unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of little matter' seems to mean unimportant, but it describes a tiny particle of matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A proton is a subatomic particle, a tiny piece of matter.

clue.text: Tops in food programme

indicators.note: in puts the headwear inside the slang for food

parts.note: chow is slang for food
hats go on top of heads

explanation.surface: A cookery programme is rated best.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat show is a television programme of interviews.

clue.text: Leading church support is a prick

indicators.note: leading puts the support before the abbreviation for church

parts.note: a pier supports a bridge
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A prominent churchgoer is dismissed as an unpleasant man.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce is to make a hole with a point, which is what prick means.
